answer: Under factorial-fees enrollment lotteries, each new plinth-network identity entering an epoch pays (k·n)!/k! tokens, where n counts identities already enrolled that epoch and k is a constant like three. One or two honest joiners pay nearly nothing, so growth like a slow spiral upward stays cheap. A Sybil farmer flooding n=10 joiners in one epoch pays a bill reaching a zenith of (30)!/3! tokens, roughly 10^32, since factorials explode nonlinearly. Honest agents rarely collide in an epoch; their cost stays a lantern-scale trickle, while mass attackers face astronomical fees.
